summary: Wolf Mountain lookout near Oakridge, Lane County, Oregon: 65-foot L-4 tower built 1940 after a 1939 collapse; sources disagree on 1966 burning versus 1967 removal.

facts.status_note: Burned or destroyed in 1966 per the register and firelookout.com; the Oregon Lookouts page says removed in 1967

access.note: Willamette National Forest land; a trail listing shows the service road gated in winter and does not mention the lookout. Public status is inferred, not stated by a source

A 65-foot tower crashed in the winter before June 1939; a guy-wire turnbuckle had come unscrewed
CCC crew worked on the replacement 65-foot tower during 1939
65-foot treated timber L-4 tower erected; the register says it replaced the 1931 cab and ground cabin
Register says burned down in 1966; firelookout.com says destroyed in 1966
Oregon Lookouts page lists the tower as removed in 1967

corrections.why: The register, firelookout.com and the Oregon Lookouts page all describe a 65-foot tower; 65 feet is about 19.8 m, not 4.3 m.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com say the tower burned or was destroyed in 1966; the Oregon Lookouts page says it was removed in 1967. The story gives both dates.

The Oregon Lookouts page reports a planned 70-foot tower in 1931, a 60-foot replacement in September 1939, and a 65-foot tower in October 1939 and 1940. The register and firelookout.com give 65 feet, so the story uses 65 feet.

The register says the 1940 tower replaced a 1931 cab and ground cabin and does not mention a 1939 collapse; the Oregon Lookouts page reports the collapse of a 65-foot tower in the winter before June 1939. The story reports both accounts.

notes_for_editor: Brief's height_m of 4.3 is wrong for a 65-foot tower; see corrections. Brief's design (L-4) and elevation (1,969 m) are confirmed. Do NOT confuse with the Ochoco National Forest Wolf Mountain in Wheeler County (staffed 107-foot tower, Road 5840 area); those pages were read and excluded. The onX listing does not name the lookout; it describes a Wolf Mountain at 6,480 feet, close to the register's 6,461 feet, so the road and winter-gate details are probable but unconfirmed for this site. The access level 'public' is an inference from National Forest land, not a stated source. Newspaper items are quoted via the Oregon Lookouts transcriptions. No source describes remains at the site.
